trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Lisbon, Portugal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour
experiences.description: Spend a culinary afternoon at Lisbon's iconic food market sampling the best of Portuguese cuisine. Try bacalhau à Brás (salted codfish), pastéis de nata from the famous Manteigaria stall, piri-piri chicken, and local cheeses paired with Vinho Verde. Chat with local vendors to learn about traditional ingredients and cooking methods.

experiences.name: Belém Historical Monuments & Pastéis de Belém
experiences.description: Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery and the iconic Tower of Belém, both masterpieces of Manueline architecture dating to the Age of Discovery. Afterward, stop at the legendary Pastéis de Belém bakery, open since 1837, for the original custard tarts made from a secret recipe. Explore the nearby Monument to the Discoveries along the Tagus riverfront.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Metro (Linha Vermelha/Red Line) from Aeroporto station directly into the city center. Affordable at ~€1.65 with a Viva Viagem card.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Lisbon City Stay and freshen up. Then take a leisurely walk through Baixa-Chiado, Lisbon's historic downtown grid. Explore Praça do Comércio by the Tagus riverfront, stroll through Rua Augusta pedestrian street, and soak in the city atmosphere at no cost.
day_by_day.evening: Head up to the Alfama district for a gentle evening wander. Climb to the Miradouro das Portas do Sol viewpoint for a free panoramic sunset view over the terracotta rooftops and the Tagus River. A perfect low-cost introduction to Lisbon's soul.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick pastel de nata and coffee at a local café near the airport or metro station for under €2.
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh sandwich or bifana (pork roll) from a local tasca near Baixa for €2–4.
meals.dinner: Dine at a traditional tasca in Alfama such as Tasca do Chico or similar neighborhood spots. Look for the prato do dia (daily special) which typically includes soup, main, and bread for €7–10.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a reloadable Viva Viagem card at the airport Metro station (€0.50 card fee). Load enough credit for a few days of travel. Keep arrival day light — jet lag and transit can be tiring. Alfama is walkable from most central accommodations.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Alfama district in depth during the morning when it is quieter. Visit the Castelo de São Jorge (Castle of St. George) — entrance is €15 but offers sweeping city views and rich Moorish and medieval history. Arrive early to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join the Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour — an iconic culinary experience at the Mercado da Ribeira in Cais do Sodré. Sample Portugal's finest dishes including fresh seafood, petiscos (tapas), ginjinha, and pastéis de nata from top local vendors. Budget around €15–25 for tastings.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Ribeira waterfront promenade at sunset. Visit the LX Factory market area in Alcântara (open late on Saturdays) for street food, local crafts, and a vibrant atmosphere. Browse freely and grab an affordable snack.

meals.breakfast: Start the day at a local pastelaria near the hotel — coffee and pastel de nata for €1.50–2.50. A classic Portuguese breakfast.
meals.lunch: Covered by the Time Out Market food tour tastings in the afternoon — graze across multiple stalls for a full culinary experience.
meals.dinner: Head to Mercado de Campo de Ourique or a nearby tasca for a budget dinner. Try bacalhau à brás (salted cod with eggs and potatoes) for €8–12.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday at Time Out Market can be busy — arrive around 13:00–14:00 for a good experience. LX Factory is especially lively on Saturday evenings. Wear comfortable walking shoes as Alfama has steep, cobbled streets.

day_by_day.morning: Take Tram 15E or a bus from Praça da Figueira to Belém (about 20–25 minutes, €1.65). Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a breathtaking example of Manueline architecture. The main church is free to enter; the cloisters cost €10 (or €16 combined with the Tower of Belém).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Belém waterfront to the iconic Torre de Belém (Tower of Belém), another UNESCO World Heritage Site and symbol of Portugal's Age of Discovery. Combine ticket with Jerónimos for best value. Stop at the nearby Padrão dos Descobrimentos (Monument to the Discoveries) for a photo — exterior viewing is free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon via tram or bus. Spend the evening exploring the Bairro Alto neighborhood — a hub of fado music, local bars, and affordable eateries. Listen for live fado drifting from open doorways for a free cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Stop at the world-famous Pastéis de Belém bakery (original since 1837) for the authentic pastel de Belém with cinnamon and powdered sugar — €1.30 each. A must-do experience.
meals.lunch: Grab a simple lunch at a café near Belém waterfront. Try a prego (steak sandwich) or soup and bread at a local café for €4–7.
meals.dinner: Explore Bairro Alto's affordable restaurant row. Look for a menu turístico (tourist menu) offering starter, main, dessert, and drink for €10–13 at local tascas.

day_by_day.notes: Belém is about 6km west of central Lisbon. Tram 15E is the most scenic and budget-friendly option. Jerónimos Monastery may have reduced Sunday afternoon hours — check ahead. Bairro Alto comes alive after 20:00.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museu Nacional do Azulejo (National Tile Museum) — one of Lisbon's most unique and affordable cultural gems (€5 entry). Housed in a stunning former convent, it traces the history of Portugal's iconic azulejo ceramic tiles from the 15th century to today.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mouraria neighborhood — Lisbon's oldest and most multicultural quarter, birthplace of fado music. Walk the historic lanes, visit the Intendente square, and discover street art and local life. Completely free. Continue to the Graça district and visit the Miradouro da Graça for arguably the best free city viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost fado performance. Several venues in Alfama and Mouraria offer free fado nights (consumo mínimo/minimum drink purchase only). Check listings for Casa de Linhares or street fado events. This is a deeply authentic Portuguese cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Visit a neighborhood padaria (bakery) for fresh bread, butter, and coffee — budget €2–3 for a filling start.
meals.lunch: Try a workers' lunch at a local tasca in Mouraria — many offer a prato do dia with soup, bread, main, and a glass of wine for €6–9.
meals.dinner: Dine near Alfama before the fado evening. Look for grilled sardines (sardinhas grelhadas) or caldo verde (kale soup) at a simple restaurant for €8–11.

day_by_day.notes: The Azulejo Museum is closed on Mondays in some seasons — verify opening hours in advance and swap with another activity if needed. Mouraria is very walkable and safe during the day. For fado venues, arrive early as popular spots fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Feira da Ladra flea market at Campo de Santa Clara (open Tuesday and Saturday mornings, free entry). Browse antiques, vintage items, local crafts, and second-hand goods — a great window into everyday Lisbon life and culture. Pick up an affordable souvenir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Parque das Nações (Park of Nations) — Lisbon's modern riverside district built for Expo 98. Walk along the Tagus promenade, admire the Ponte Vasco da Gama, and visit the exterior of the Oceanarium (exterior free; interior €21 if budget allows). The area showcases a completely different, contemporary side of Lisbon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon for a final evening. Revisit a favorite neighborhood — perhaps Chiado or Baixa — for last-minute souvenir shopping at affordable local shops. Enjoy a farewell dinner with a glass of Portuguese wine and a toast to the trip.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the Feira da Ladra area — street vendors sell coffee and snacks. Budget €2–3.
meals.lunch: Try a bifana or croquete sandwich from a local snack bar near Parque das Nações for €3–5. Many affordable café options line the waterfront promenade.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for the farewell meal — visit a well-regarded tasca in Chiado or Bairro Alto. Order bacalhau com natas or arroz de pato (duck rice) with a glass of vinho verde for €12–16 total.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure logistics today — Lisbon Airport is easily reached by Metro Red Line from Oriente station (near Parque das Nações), making this day's location very practical if flying out the next morning. Keep receipts for any VAT refund claims on purchases over €50.

trip_options.title: Classic Lisbon, Portugal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, clear customs, and take the Aerobus or Metro (Red Line to Green Line) into the city center. Check in to Lisbon City Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a relaxed self-guided stroll through the Baixa-Chiado neighborhood — Lisbon's historic downtown grid. Walk along Rua Augusta, pass through the triumphal arch to Praça do Comércio overlooking the Tagus River, and ride the iconic Elevador de Santa Justa for panoramic views over the city rooftops.
day_by_day.evening: Alfama District Walking Tour & Fado Experience — join an early-evening guided tour through Lisbon's oldest medieval neighborhood, winding through narrow alleyways past tiled facades, miradouros (viewpoints), and the São Jorge Castle walls, culminating in an authentic Fado music performance at a traditional casa de fado.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick pastel de nata and espresso (bica) at a café near the airport or hotel upon arrival — try A Padaria Portuguesa for a casual, affordable bite.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Baixa — Solar dos Presuntos takeaway counter or a tasca offering the daily prato do dia (dish of the day) for €10–13, such as bacalhau à brás or grilled chicken.
meals.dinner: Dinner included or paired with the Fado experience; alternatively dine beforehand at Tasca do Chico in Alfama — a beloved neighborhood spot with petiscos (Portuguese tapas) and grilled fish for €15–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep the pace light. Validate your Viva Viagem transport card at the airport Metro station for easy travel all week. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for Alfama's steep cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Belém Historical Monuments & Pastéis de Belém — take Tram 15E or the train from Cais do Sodré westward to Belém. Begin with the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a breathtaking example of Manueline architecture built to celebrate Portugal's Age of Discovery. Explore the ornate double-cloistered courtyard and the church where Vasco da Gama is entombed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Belém with a visit to the iconic Tower of Belém (Torre de Belém) standing sentinel on the Tagus riverbank, then walk along the waterfront promenade to the Monument to the Discoveries (Padrão dos Descobrimentos). Enjoy sweeping river views before heading back toward the city center.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon and explore the bohemian Bairro Alto neighborhood. Browse independent shops and galleries as they open for the evening, then settle into a relaxed dinner followed by a walk through the lively Príncipe Real garden square.

meals.breakfast: Stop at the legendary Pastéis de Belém bakery (open since 1837) for the original custard tarts fresh from the oven with cinnamon and powdered sugar — a non-negotiable Lisbon ritual. €1.20 per tart with a coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Belém at Café In — a relaxed riverside café offering Portuguese sandwiches, salads, and daily specials for €10–15. Alternatively, picnic with local cheeses and charcuterie from a nearby deli along the waterfront.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Bairro Alto at Taberna da Rua das Flores — a celebrated modern tasca with seasonal Portuguese small plates and natural wines, budget €25–35 per person. Reserve ahead on Sundays.

day_by_day.notes: Jerónimos Monastery is closed on Mondays, so visiting today (Sunday) is ideal. Arrive early (before 10:00) to beat crowds. The Tower of Belém can have queues — consider pre-booking online. Belém is about 6 km from the city center; the 15E tram is scenic but slow — the train from Cais do Sodré is faster.

day_by_day.morning: National Museum of Ancient Art & Chiado Cultural Stroll — spend the morning at the Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga (MNAA), Portugal's most important art museum. Highlights include Hieronymus Bosch's 'The Temptation of Saint Anthony,' Portuguese gold and silverwork, and an extensive collection of azulejo tile art. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk uphill through the elegant Chiado district — Lisbon's cultural and literary heart. Visit the historic Livraria Bertrand (world's oldest operating bookshop), browse the boutiques on Rua Garrett, and pop into the Igreja do Carmo (Carmelite Church ruins turned archaeological museum) for a unique Gothic skeleton-filled interior with open sky above.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Cais do Sodré waterfront and the Pink Street (Rua Nova do Carvalho) area as the city comes alive after dark. Enjoy live music at a bar or simply walk along the Ribeira waterfront promenade watching the Tagus at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Café A Brasileira in Chiado — a famous 1905 Art Nouveau café beloved by poets and intellectuals. Coffee and pastry for €4–6.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Time Out Market (a preview of tomorrow's full experience) or at O Corvo in Intendente — a beloved neighborhood lunch spot with hearty Portuguese daily specials for €9–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Zé da Mouraria — an unpretentious, cash-only local gem near Mouraria serving generous portions of grilled fish, caldo verde soup, and house wine for €15–20 per person. Arrive early as it fills fast.

day_by_day.notes: The MNAA is closed on Mondays — check the official website to confirm opening hours closer to travel date and consider swapping this activity to Tuesday if needed. The Chiado stroll is always accessible. Wear layers as Lisbon in May can be breezy in the mornings.

day_by_day.morning: Mouraria & Intendente Neighborhood Food & History Walk — join a guided morning tour through Lisbon's most multicultural and historically layered quarter. Explore the Moorish-origin streets where Fado was born, visit the Largo do Intendente square with its ornate tiled pharmacy facade, learn about the neighborhood's immigrant communities, and sample local street food along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour — spend a culinary afternoon at the iconic Mercado da Ribeira food hall. Sample the best of Portuguese cuisine across multiple vendors: from bifanas (pork sandwiches) and grilled octopus to artisan cheeses, ginjinha liqueur shots, and experimental modern Portuguese dishes. A structured tasting tour maximizes the experience.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Graça neighborhood — one of Lisbon's highest and most authentic residential hilltop areas. Visit the Miradouro da Graça viewpoint for golden-hour panoramas over the city and river, then wander the quiet streets lined with tiled houses before a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast near the hotel — try Mercearia do Intendente, a charming neighborhood deli-café with fresh bread, local cheeses, and coffee for €5–8, perfectly located near the morning tour start.
meals.lunch: Lunch is embedded in the Time Out Market Food Tour experience — multiple tastings across vendors included. Budget an additional €10–15 for extra dishes or drinks you want to try independently.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Graça at Páteo 13 — a hidden courtyard restaurant beloved by locals for its charcoal-grilled fish, ameijoas (clams), and cold Sagres beer in a relaxed alfresco setting. Expect €20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Mouraria tour and Time Out Market tour can be booked back-to-back as a full food-and-history day. Wear comfortable shoes — Mouraria's streets are hilly and uneven. The Time Out Market is busiest on weekends; Tuesday afternoon is a great time to visit without overwhelming crowds. Bring cash for some market vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Slow, leisurely final morning — revisit a favorite neighborhood or explore something missed earlier in the week. Consider visiting the São Vicente de Fora Monastery and its spectacular rooftop azulejo tile panels overlooking the Alfama rooftops and the Tagus. Alternatively, browse the Feira da Ladra flea market (open Tuesdays and Saturdays — if this falls on a weekend, prioritize it).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in Baixa and Chiado — pick up Portuguese ceramics, azulejo tiles, local wines, ginjinha, or sardine tins from specialty shops. Visit the Conserveira de Lisboa (a historic tinned fish shop since 1930) on Rua dos Bacalhoeiros for beautifully packaged sardines and tuna as edible souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in the Príncipe Real neighborhood — Lisbon's most refined and relaxed upscale residential quarter. Splurge slightly on a final memorable meal before packing and preparing for departure.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at a neighborhood pastelaria — order a torrada (thick buttered toast), fresh orange juice, and a galão (milky espresso) for a quintessentially Portuguese send-off. Budget €4–7.
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at Taberna Sal Grosso near Alfama — rustic, honest Portuguese cooking with daily fish and meat options for €12–18 per person. Great value and authentically local.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Tasca do Chafariiz in Príncipe Real — a refined but relaxed wine bar and restaurant specializing in Portuguese small plates, regional cheeses, charcuterie, and an exceptional wine list. Budget €30–40 per person for a memorable final evening.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your flight is in the evening. Lisbon Airport is easily reachable via Metro (Green Line to Red Line) in about 30–40 minutes from the city center. Allow at least 2 hours before departure for check-in and security. Consider downloading the CP train app and Carris bus app for seamless navigation throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer arranged from the airport to Lisbon City Stay hotel. Take time to check in, freshen up, and settle into your luxury accommodations.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely stroll through the elegant Chiado and Bairro Alto neighborhoods near the hotel. Browse upscale boutiques, admire the iconic Livraria Bertrand (the world's oldest operating bookshop), and soak in the atmosphere of one of Lisbon's most refined districts. Stop at a traditional miradouro (viewpoint) such as Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara for panoramic views over the city.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Lisbon's culinary scene with a reservation at Belcanto, Chef José Avillez's two-Michelin-star flagship restaurant in Chiado. Indulge in an exquisite tasting menu celebrating contemporary Portuguese haute cuisine with seasonal ingredients and masterful technique. After dinner, enjoy a digestif at a sophisticated cocktail bar nearby such as Park Bar rooftop for stunning city views.

meals.lunch: Light welcome snack and refreshments upon hotel arrival — ask the concierge to arrange a curated cheese, charcuterie, and wine spread in your room featuring Portuguese specialties like Serra da Estrela cheese and presunto.
meals.dinner: Belcanto (Rua Serpa Pinto, Chiado) — Michelin two-star tasting menu featuring modern Portuguese cuisine. Reserve the chef's tasting menu with optional wine pairing of premium Douro and Alentejo wines.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance through the hotel concierge. Given the 13:00 arrival, allow at least 90 minutes for immigration, baggage, and transfer before reaching the hotel. Confirm Belcanto reservation well in advance as it books up months ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the day with the Alfama District Walking Tour & Fado Experience. Join a private guided tour through Lisbon's oldest and most atmospheric neighborhood, winding through medieval alleyways, past the imposing São Jorge Castle, and down to the ancient Sé Cathedral. Your expert guide will narrate centuries of Moorish, Christian, and maritime history etched into the neighborhood's cobblestones and azulejo-tiled facades.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Alfama at your own pace after the guided portion concludes. Visit the Museu do Fado to deepen your understanding of Portugal's soulful musical tradition before heading to the Miradouro da Graça or Miradouro da Senhora do Monte for the finest panoramic views of Lisbon's rooftops and the Tagus River. Return to the hotel for a mid-afternoon rest.
day_by_day.evening: Experience an authentic and intimate Fado performance as part of the evening extension of your Alfama experience. Dine at Zé da Mouraria or book a table at the prestigious Casa de Linhares, a 16th-century palace in Alfama that hosts world-class Fado performances alongside a premium Portuguese dinner. Sip aged Tawny Port between performances for the full sensory experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel's restaurant — enjoy a lavish spread of freshly baked pastries, smoked salmon, artisan cheeses, tropical fruits, and freshly squeezed orange juice paired with a bica (Portuguese espresso).
meals.lunch: Taberna da Rua das Flores in Chiado — a beloved upscale tasca serving traditional petiscos (Portuguese tapas) such as bacalhau à brás, amêijoas à Bulhão Pato (clams), and presunto with melon. Natural wine list is excellent.
meals.dinner: Casa de Linhares (Beco dos Armazéns do Linho, Alfama) — a romantic Fado dinner venue set inside a historic palace. Enjoy a multi-course Portuguese dinner with live Fado performances by acclaimed fadistas.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Alfama cobblestone streets. The neighborhood involves steep inclines — consider the private tour option which can include a tuk-tuk segment for less mobile guests. Book Casa de Linhares well in advance for weekend evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to the Belém Historical Monuments & Pastéis de Belém experience. Take a private chauffeured transfer to Belém along the scenic Tagus riverside. Begin with the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a breathtaking masterpiece of Manueline Gothic architecture built to celebrate Vasco da Gama's discovery of the sea route to India. Explore the ornate cloisters, royal tombs, and soaring nave with a private guide who will illuminate the Age of Discovery history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the iconic Tower of Belém, standing sentinel on the Tagus River since 1519. Afterward, visit the Monument to the Discoveries (Padrão dos Descobrimentos) and the Museu de Arte, Arquitetura e Tecnologia (MAAT) for a striking contrast of historical and contemporary culture. End the afternoon with a visit to the legendary Pastéis de Belém bakery for the original pastel de nata custard tarts, a recipe kept secret since 1837.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon and enjoy a sophisticated dinner in the upscale Príncipe Real neighborhood. Book a table at Antiqvm or Alma (Chef Henrique Sá Pessoa's Michelin-starred restaurant in Chiado) for an elevated interpretation of Portuguese culinary heritage. Round off the evening with a glass of vintage Madeira wine at a wine bar in Príncipe Real.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast followed by the iconic pastéis de nata at Pastéis de Belém (Rua de Belém 84) — pair the warm, flaky custard tarts with a bica coffee. A quintessential Lisbon morning ritual.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Solar dos Presuntos (Rossio area) or picnic-style lunch curated by the hotel concierge with premium Portuguese provisions — artisan bread, aged cheese, charcuterie, olives, and local wine enjoyed at the Belém riverside gardens.
meals.dinner: Alma Restaurant (Rua Anchieta, Chiado) — Chef Henrique Sá Pessoa's Michelin-starred restaurant offering a refined tasting menu that reimagines classic Portuguese flavors with modern elegance. Exceptional Portuguese wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: Belém is approximately 6–7 km from central Lisbon. Arrange a private chauffeured car or luxury taxi for the day. Sunday mornings can be busy at Jerónimos Monastery — a private guided tour with skip-the-line access is strongly recommended. The pastéis de nata queue at Pastéis de Belém moves quickly despite appearances.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at the National Museum of Ancient Art (Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga) & Chiado Cultural Stroll. Begin at Portugal's most important art museum, housing masterpieces including Hieronymus Bosch's 'The Temptation of Saint Anthony' triptych, Nuno Gonçalves' polyptych panels, and an extraordinary collection of Portuguese decorative arts, silver, ceramics, and textiles spanning five centuries. A private guided tour will provide rich historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on the Mouraria & Intendente Neighborhood Food & History Walk. Discover Lisbon's multicultural soul in Mouraria, the ancient Moorish quarter and birthplace of Fado. A knowledgeable local guide will lead you through hidden squares, community gardens, and heritage sites while introducing you to the neighborhood's layered history — from Moorish occupation to contemporary immigrant communities. Sample local street food and specialty products along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed but indulgent evening at one of Lisbon's most celebrated wine bars. Visit By the Wine (David Baverstock) in Chiado for an expertly curated selection of Portuguese wines by the glass, paired with premium petiscos. Afterward, treat yourself to a nightcap at TOPO Chiado rooftop bar for sweeping views of the castle and city lights over the Tagus.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — opt for the à la carte menu and request a selection of traditional Portuguese breads (pão de Deus, broa) with local honey, butter, and seasonal fruit alongside a galão coffee.
meals.lunch: During the Mouraria food walk, sample authentic petiscos at local tascas recommended by your guide. Highlights may include bifanas (pork sandwiches), caldo verde soup, and local wines. Supplement with a sit-down lunch at Zé da Mouraria for hearty traditional Portuguese fare.
meals.dinner: Tasca do Chico (Rua do Diário de Notícias, Bairro Alto) — an intimate, reservation-only tasca beloved by Lisbon insiders. Exceptional petiscos, natural wines, and occasional spontaneous Fado performances. Book far in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Ancient Art is closed on Mondays — if this is the case, substitute the morning with a private visit to the Museu Calouste Gulbenkian, one of Europe's finest private art collections, or the Museu Nacional do Azulejo (Tile Museum) for an immersive exploration of Portugal's iconic decorative tile tradition. Always verify museum opening hours with the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Start the final morning with a leisurely visit to the Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour for a premium culinary send-off. Spend the morning at Lisbon's iconic food market in Cais do Sodré, sampling the finest offerings from the market's curated selection of top chefs and artisan producers. Highlights include Michelin-chef counters, artisan pastries, Portuguese cheeses, charcuterie, and freshly shucked oysters paired with Vinho Verde.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Príncipe Real neighborhood for a final afternoon of leisure. Browse the upscale antique shops and design boutiques along Rua Dom Pedro V, visit the beautiful Jardim do Príncipe Real garden, and pick up premium Portuguese souvenirs — artisan ceramics, aged ginjinha (cherry liqueur), single-origin olive oils, or a bottle of vintage Port wine. Stop for a final bica at one of the neighborhood's charming café terraces.
day_by_day.evening: Conclude your Lisbon journey with a grand farewell dinner at Bairro do Avillez (Chef José Avillez's premium brasserie in Chiado) or at Loco, a Michelin-starred avant-garde restaurant offering a bold, creative tasting menu. Toast to an unforgettable trip with a glass of aged Colheita Port or a premium Douro red. Arrange a private transfer back to the hotel and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — indulge in the full luxury spread one last time. Request a special farewell amenity from the concierge such as a bottle of Champagne or a selection of premium Portuguese pastries.
meals.lunch: Time Out Market Lisbon — graze across multiple premium counters. Recommended stops: Alexandre Silva's counter for creative Portuguese dishes, Henrique Sá Pessoa's stall, and the oyster bar. Pair with a glass of crisp Alvarinho white wine.
meals.dinner: Loco Restaurant (Rua dos Navegantes, Estrela) — Chef Alexandre Silva's Michelin-starred tasting menu pushing the boundaries of Portuguese cuisine with inventive technique and local seasonal ingredients. A memorable and fitting finale to a luxury Lisbon trip.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight time and arrange private airport transfer through the hotel concierge. Time Out Market is best visited mid-morning before the lunch crowds arrive. If departing early the following morning, consider requesting a late checkout or packing the night before to allow a relaxed final evening. Ask the hotel to prepare a farewell gift bag of Portuguese delicacies for the journey home.
